label: Pair representation and the triangle update
context: Left: 7 residues drawn as circles on a curved chain. Right: a 7×7 grid, the pair representation z_ij, cells shaded by a predicted distance (dark = close). Phase 1: hover across residue pairs; a line between residue i and j on the left highlights cell (i, j) on the right; caption 'z_ij: one feature vector for every pair'. Phase 2 'triangle update': pick i and j, then sweep k across all residues; for each k draw the triangle i–j–k on the left (edges coloured) and highlight cells (i, k) and (j, k) on the grid with arrows into (i, j); caption 'if i is near k and k is near j, then i is near j: z_ij is updated from z_ik and z_jk for every k'. Phase 3: the whole grid refreshes, becoming more consistent (noise in the shading decreases). Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: Pair representation and the triangle update
spec.caption: Each pair of residues (i, j) owns a feature vector zᵢⱼ. The triangle update refreshes zᵢⱼ from zᵢₖ and zⱼₖ for every third residue k, and the whole grid becomes more consistent.
